When approval is needed, the caller must approve the SpotPool contract before submitting the order transaction. Without sufficient allowance the on-chain transaction will revert. "marginBank" places against MarginBank collateral and is valid **only** on perpetual (`kind: "perp"`) markets; the pool locks initial margin from the account's free collateral at placement. reserved from the wallet at placement. Fills still execute at

post.description:
Generates a standard ERC-20 `approve(marginBank, amount)` transaction
authorizing the MarginBank contract to pull collateral from the caller's
wallet. The transaction targets the **collateral token** contract, not
MarginBank, because ERC-20 approve is called on the token itself.

Required before `POST /v0/account/margin/deposit`.

This mirrors the spot `POST /v0/markets/{symbol}/vault/approve` response
shape, including its JSON `null` case. In practice MarginBank collateral
is always an ERC-20 (USDso) with no native-token equivalent of the spot
vault's `depositNative()`, so the `null` branch is unreachable today; it
is kept so both approve endpoints decode identically.

Generates an unsigned `MarginBank.deposit(amount)` transaction moving
collateral from the caller's wallet into the shared margin account.

MarginBank collateral is **account-level, not per-market**: a single
balance backs every perpetual position the wallet holds, which is why
this route lives under `/v0/account` rather than under a symbol. The
collateral token is fixed at deployment (USDso), so no `currency` is
needed.

The MarginBank contract must hold sufficient ERC-20 allowance first —
see `POST /v0/account/margin/approve`.

Deposits are unconditional; withdrawals are not (see the withdraw
endpoint).

Generates an unsigned `MarginBank.withdraw(amount)` transaction moving
free collateral from the shared margin account back to the caller's
wallet.

Only **free** collateral can be withdrawn — margin locked against open
positions or resting orders cannot. The transaction is encoded blindly
with no server-side margin preflight, so a withdrawal that would breach
the account's initial-margin requirement reverts on-chain
(`InsufficientMarginAfterWithdrawal`) rather than failing here.
Simulate with `eth_call` before submitting.

get.description:
Returns the given wallet's cross-market collateral ledger (margin
deposits/withdrawals, realized PnL, fees, funding), newest-first,
cursor-paginated. The wallet is taken from the path verbatim - no
linked-wallet group resolution.

Any authenticated caller may read their own wallet. Reading a
different wallet requires the `wallet:read_any` scope; without it,
requesting another wallet returns 403 and an unauthenticated
request returns 401.

post.description:
Authenticates a user by verifying a signed ERC-4361 (Sign-In with Ethereum)
message. The message must include a valid nonce obtained from the /auth/nonce
endpoint. Returns a JWT bearer token for authenticating subsequent requests.
The token should be included in the Authorization header as "Bearer <token>".

get.description:
Returns a cryptographically random nonce for use in Sign-In with Ethereum
(ERC-4361) authentication. The nonce is single-use and expires after 5 minutes.
Include this nonce in your SIWE message when authenticating.

Returns all currencies (tokens and assets) supported by this exchange.
Each currency includes its identifier, ticker code, and display name.
Use this endpoint to discover which assets are available for trading
and to populate currency selection interfaces.

Returns recent liquidations across all perpetual markets, newest-first,
cursor-paginated. Each entry carries its market symbol.

Returns all trading pairs (markets) available on this exchange. Each market
includes its symbol identifier along with base and quote currency information.
Use this endpoint to discover tradeable pairs and to populate market selection
interfaces. Markets are identified by symbols in the format "BASE:QUOTE"
(e.g., "SOMI:USDso").

Returns the builder approval the authenticated wallet has granted for a
specific builder, in BPS_TIMES_1K units. `approved` is the raw value the
wallet granted (which may exceed the current protocol cap); `effective`
is `min(approved, protocolMaxFee)` — the rate the chain actually enforces
at order placement.

post.description:
Generates an unsigned EVM transaction calling `approveBuilder` on the
SpotPool, granting a builder permission to charge a per-fill fee (up to
`maxFeeBpsTimes1k`) on orders the authenticated wallet submits with that
builder code. The transaction targets the pool and must be signed and
broadcast by the wallet.

Builder approval is keyed on the **order owner** (the signing wallet),
not the order submitter. A wallet must approve a builder before it can
place orders tagged with that builder via the `builder` field on
`POST /v0/markets/{symbol}/orders`.

Set `maxFeeBpsTimes1k` to `0` to revoke an existing approval. The
approval is also bounded by the protocol-wide cap
(`GET /v0/markets/{symbol}/builder/max-fee`); a value above the cap is
rejected on-chain.

get.description:
Returns the protocol-wide cap on per-user builder approvals for this
market's pool, in BPS_TIMES_1K units. A value of `0` means builder
codes are disabled for the pool.

Returns historical OHLCV (Open, High, Low, Close, Volume) candlestick data
for charting purposes. Each candle represents price action over a specific
time interval. This endpoint supports various timeframes and is essential
for rendering price charts and performing technical analysis.

To page backwards through history, supply `endTime` as a unix millisecond
timestamp. Only candles whose bucket timestamp is strictly less than
`endTime` are returned. Combined with `limit`, this lets a client load
successive older windows by passing the oldest returned timestamp as the
next request's `endTime`.

Returns the current funding state plus a paginated funding-rate history
for a perpetual market, newest-first. 404 for spot symbols. The
`nextCursor` token pages the history.

Returns the authenticated wallet's per-account funding settlements for
a perpetual market, newest-first, cursor-paginated. 404 for spot
symbols.

post.description:
Generates an unsigned `MarginBank.setMaxLeverage(perpPool, leverageX)`
transaction capping the caller's leverage on one perpetual market.

Perp-only: returns `404` for a spot symbol. The call lives on MarginBank
(which owns margin accounting) rather than on the pool, but is scoped
per-market via the pool address the server resolves from `{symbol}`.

The cap governs **subsequent** orders — it is consulted when an order's
initial margin is quoted. Setting it is a plain settings write with no
margin check, so it never reverts on account of an open position, and an
existing position is neither re-margined nor liquidated. Lowering the cap
below a position's current effective leverage is permitted; the account
simply cannot add to that position until it is back within the cap.

On-chain rejections are limited to: an unregistered perp pool
(`InvalidPerpPool`), a `leverage` of zero or above the protocol-wide
limit (`InvalidLeverage`), a value equal to the one already stored
(`NoStateChange`), and a credit-voucher account whose leverage is locked
(`VoucherAccountLeverageLocked`).

get.description:
Returns the liquidation feed for a perpetual market, newest-first,
cursor-paginated. 404 for spot symbols.

Returns current open interest plus a paginated OI history for a
perpetual market, newest-first. 404 for spot symbols.

Returns orders for the authenticated account in a specific market,
newest-first. Orders can be filtered by status (open, closed, canceled,
expired, rejected) using the optional status query parameter. Each
order includes its current state, fill progress, and associated
transaction hash. The response includes a `nextCursor` token when
more pages are available — pass it back as `cursor` to continue.

post.description:
Generates an unsigned EVM transaction for placing a new order on-chain.
The response contains the transaction payload (to, data, value, chainId)
that must be signed and broadcast by the client's wallet. This non-custodial
approach ensures the server never handles private keys. Supports both
market orders (immediate execution at best price) and limit orders
(execution at specified price or better).

For conditional stop orders, see `POST /v0/markets/{symbol}/stop-orders`.

### Validation rules

A request that fails these checks returns `400` with a field-specific
`name` (also mirrored in the `Error-Name` header):

- `price` (limit orders) must be greater than zero and an exact multiple
  of the market's `tickSize`, else `invalid_price`.
- `amount` must be an exact multiple of the market's `lotSize` and at
  least its `minQuantity`, else `invalid_amount`. There is no minimum
  order value (notional).
- A required field omitted from the body returns `missing_field`; a body
  that is malformed or has a field of the wrong type returns
  `invalid_request_body`.

### Spot and perpetual markets

The same route places orders on both market kinds — a perp pool inherits
the identical `placeOrder(...)` entry point, so the request body shape is
unchanged. What differs is the funding source, which must match the
symbol's `kind`:

| Market `kind` | Valid `fundingSource` |
|---|---|
| `spot` | `wallet` (default), `vault` |
| `perp` | `marginBank` |

A mismatch is rejected with `400 invalid_param`. On a perp market the
pool locks initial margin from the account's free MarginBank collateral
at placement, so fund it first via `POST /v0/account/margin/deposit`;
there is no per-order ERC-20 approval on the perp path, and the
`approval` response field is never present.

### Token approval for wallet funding source

When using `fundingSource: "wallet"`, the SpotPool contract must have
sufficient ERC-20 allowance to pull tokens from the caller's wallet.
The server checks the caller's current on-chain allowance and only
includes an `approval` field in the response when additional approval
is needed. If `approval` is absent, the existing allowance already
covers the order and the caller can submit the order transaction
directly.

When `approval` is present, the caller must submit a
`token.approve(spotPoolAddress, amount)` transaction **before** sending
the order transaction. For **buy** orders, approve the **quote** token
(you spend quote to buy base). For **sell** orders, approve the **base**
token. Use `POST /v0/markets/{symbol}/vault/approve` to generate the
approve transaction. The `approval.amount` covers the order cost plus
taker fee overhead from ceiling rounding.

**Note:** Market buy orders with `fundingSource: "wallet"` are priced
off the live best ask plus `slippageBps` (default 5%), which bounds the
quote pulled from the wallet. They return a 400 error only when the ask
side is empty (no liquidity to price against). Fills execute at resting
maker prices, so `slippageBps` only widens how deep the order sweeps and
the approval headroom, not the price paid.

### Recommended workflow

1. **Simulate before submitting.** Call the returned transaction via
   `eth_call` before sending it. The `placeOrder` function returns
   `(bool success, uint256 orderId)`. If `success` is `false`, the
   order will be rejected on-chain -- do not submit the transaction.
2. **Sign and broadcast.** If the simulation returns `success = true`,
   sign the transaction and send it.
3. **Verify after confirmation.** Once the transaction confirms, check
   the receipt logs for the `OrderPlaced` event. If the logs array is
   empty, the order was silently rejected.

### Why an order can be rejected

A `placeOrder` transaction can succeed (receipt `status = 1`) yet not
actually place an order. When this happens the call returns
`(false, 0)` and emits no events. This occurs when the order passes
basic validation (price, quantity, lot size) but is rejected for a
runtime reason such as:

- The order expired before execution
- It would match against the sender's own resting order (self-trade)
- A PostOnly order would have filled immediately
- A FillOrKill order could not be completely filled
- An ImmediateOrCancel order found nothing to fill against

delete.description:
Generates an unsigned EVM transaction for canceling an open order.
Only orders with status "open" can be canceled. The response contains
the transaction payload (to, data, value, chainId) that must be signed
and broadcast by the client's wallet. Once confirmed on-chain, the
order is canceled and any unfilled portion is returned to the vault.

Works on both spot and perpetual markets: a perp pool inherits the same
`cancelOrder(orderId)` entry point, so the request and response shapes
are identical. On a perp market the released amount is margin returned
to the account's free MarginBank collateral rather than to a spot vault.

get.description:
Returns detailed information about a specific order by its unique identifier.
The response includes the order's current status, original parameters,
fill progress (filled vs remaining amounts), and the on-chain transaction
hash if available. Use this endpoint to poll for order status updates
or display order details.

patch.description:
Prepares a transaction to reduce an open order to a specified remaining
quantity. The newQuantityRemaining must be less than or equal to the
current remaining quantity, at least minQuantity, and a multiple of
lotSize. The order's fullQuantity and quantityRemaining are both
decreased by the difference.

Works on both spot and perpetual markets: a perp pool inherits the same
`reduceOrder(orderId, newQuantityRemaining)` entry point, so the request
and response shapes are identical. On a perp market the freed amount is
margin released back to the account's free MarginBank collateral.

get.description:
Returns current positions across all accounts on a perpetual market,
cursor-paginated. Restricted to bearer tokens carrying the
`positions:read_any` scope; tokens without it receive 403. 404 for spot
symbols.

Returns the authenticated wallet's current position in a perpetual
market, or null when the wallet has no open position. 404 for spot
symbols.

Returns the given wallet's current position in a perpetual market, or
null when the wallet has no open position. Restricted to bearer tokens
carrying the `positions:read_any` scope; tokens without it receive 403.
404 for spot symbols.

Returns the authenticated user's pending stop orders for the given
market. Optionally filter by status (pending, triggered, canceled,
failed). Orders are returned newest-first.

post.description:
Generates an unsigned EVM transaction for creating a conditional stop
order on the SpotStopOrderRegistry. Stop orders are held off-book until
a mark-price trigger condition is met, then automatically placed as an
ImmediateOrCancel (IOC) order on the CLOB.

The `triggerOperator` field controls the trigger direction:
- **gte** -- triggers when mark price >= triggerPrice (stop-buy, take-profit)
- **lte** -- triggers when mark price <= triggerPrice (stop-loss)

Each stop order executes as either:
- **market** -- triggers at mark price +/- the registry's slippage tolerance
- **limit** -- triggers at the caller-specified limit price

The response `value` field contains the required SOMI payment that
funds the on-chain reactivity handler. SOMI is refunded on
cancellation and consumed when the order triggers.

**Operator approval is a prerequisite.** The wallet must first grant the
market's stop-order registry permission to place orders on its behalf,
otherwise this endpoint returns `400 operator_approval_required`. Check
status with `GET /v0/markets/{symbol}/stop-orders/authorization` and
generate the one-time grant transaction with
`POST /v0/markets/{symbol}/stop-orders/approve`.

Funds are NOT escrowed at creation time. The user must have sufficient
balance deposited in the vault when the order triggers. If the balance
is insufficient at trigger time, the order fails gracefully and is
removed from the registry.

### Validation rules

- `triggerPrice` must be greater than zero
- `amount` must be >= the market's minQuantity and a multiple of lotSize
- For **limit** type: `price` must be > 0 and a multiple of tickSize
- For **limit** type with sell + lte: `price` must be <= `triggerPrice`
- For **limit** type with buy + gte: `price` must be >= `triggerPrice`

Generates an unsigned EVM transaction granting the market's stop-order
registry operator permission to place orders on the caller's behalf, by
calling `setOperatorApprovalForPool` on the OperatorPermissionsRegistry.

This is a one-time, per-market grant and a prerequisite for creating
stop orders. The registry address is discovered on-chain from the pool,
so it always reflects the live deployment. The grant can be revoked by
the owner at any time and does not affect already-resting orders.

get.description:
Reports whether the authenticated wallet has granted the market's
stop-order registry operator permission to place orders on its behalf.

This grant is a one-time, per-market prerequisite for creating stop
orders. Call this before showing the stop-order create form; when
`authorized` is false, generate the grant transaction with
`POST /v0/markets/{symbol}/stop-orders/approve`.

delete.description:
Generates an unsigned EVM transaction for cancelling a pending stop
order on the SpotStopOrderRegistry. Only the order's owner can cancel.
On-chain cancellation refunds the SOMI payment that was attached when
the order was created.

get.description:
Returns a single stop order by its identifier. Use this to poll a stop
order's lifecycle status (pending, triggered, canceled, failed) and,
once triggered, the resting spot order id. Stop orders are public
on-chain data, so the order is returned regardless of which wallet
owns it.

Returns 24-hour OHLCV market statistics for a specific trading pair.
Includes open, high, low, close prices and total trade volume.
All fields are "0" if no trades occurred in the period.

Returns the most recent executed trades for a specific market. Each trade
includes the price, quantity, side (buy/sell), and timestamp. This data
is useful for displaying trade history feeds and analyzing recent market
activity. Trades are returned newest-first (reverse chronological order).

The endpoint is public, but callers presenting a bearer token with the
`trades:read_any` scope additionally receive the `maker` and `taker`
wallet addresses on each trade.

Returns the authenticated user's executed trades for a specific market.
Includes trades where the user was either the taker or the maker. Each
trade includes the price, quantity, side, and timestamp. Trades are
returned newest-first (reverse chronological order).

Returns executed trades for the given wallet address within a market
over a half-open time range `[since, until)`. Includes trades where
the wallet was either the taker or the maker. Trades are returned
newest-first (reverse chronological order); the response is an empty
array when no trades match.

Access is restricted to bearer tokens carrying the `trades:read_any`
scope. Tokens without the scope receive 403. Because the scope is
required, each trade always includes the `maker` and `taker` wallet
addresses.

`until` defaults to the current time if omitted; `since` defaults to
`until - 7 days`. The range must not exceed 40 days — longer ranges
return 400. Use `as=maker` or `as=taker` to restrict the result to
one side; both sides are returned by default.

post.description:
Generates a standard ERC-20 `approve(spender, amount)` transaction that
authorizes the pool contract to spend the given amount of a token on
behalf of the wallet. The transaction targets the **token** contract
(not the pool) because ERC-20 approve is called on the token itself.

This approval is required before:
- **Vault deposits** — the pool must be approved to transfer tokens into
  the vault via the deposit endpoint.
- **Wallet-funded orders** (`fundingSource: "wallet"`) — the pool must
  be approved to pull tokens for the atomic deposit-order-withdraw flow.
  The order response includes an `approval` field with the exact token
  and fee-inclusive amount needed.

For **buy** orders, approve the **quote** token (you spend quote to buy
base). For **sell** orders, approve the **base** token. The amount must
cover the order cost plus taker fee overhead from ceiling rounding.

**Native token:** when the currency is the chain's native token there
is no ERC-20 to approve — deposits use the payable `depositNative()`
entry point. In that case the endpoint responds with HTTP 200 and a
body of JSON `null`, signaling the client to skip signing and proceed
directly to the deposit endpoint.

get.description:
Returns the withdrawable balances for both the base and quote tokens in
a market's vault for the authenticated wallet. Use this to display
available funds for trading or withdrawal.

post.description:
Generates an unsigned EVM transaction for depositing tokens into the
market's vault. The caller must first approve the pool contract to spend
the token via the approve endpoint. The response contains the transaction
payload (to, data, value, chainId) that must be signed and broadcast by
the client's wallet.

Generates an unsigned EVM transaction for withdrawing tokens from the
market's vault back to the caller's wallet. The response contains the
transaction payload (to, data, value, chainId) that must be signed and
broadcast by the client's wallet.

get.description:
Returns the total trading volume for a market over a half-open time
range `[since, until)`. Volume aggregates every fill in the window
across all traders. Both scaled (human-readable) and raw (atomic token
units) figures are returned for the base and quote tokens, so callers
such as volume aggregators need no client-side decimal scaling. Resolve
token addresses and decimals via `GET /v0/markets`.

`until` defaults to 30 minutes ago when omitted; `since` defaults to
`until - 7 days`. The range must not exceed 40 days — longer ranges
return 400.

To account for ingestion latency, an explicit `until` newer than 30
minutes ago is rejected with 400; recently executed trades may not yet
be queryable.

Returns aggregated order book data for one or more market symbols.
The response includes all open bids and asks sorted by price, with
quantities at each price level. Use the optional depth parameter to
limit the number of price levels returned. Order books are essential
for displaying market depth charts and calculating slippage estimates.

If **any** requested symbol is not a known market, the whole request
is rejected with `400 invalid_param` and the offending symbols are
listed in the error's `context.invalid_symbols` array so the client
can correct their input. Fail-fast — clients see typos immediately
rather than getting a shorter list back with no way to tell why.

Returns orders for the authenticated account across one or more markets,
newest-first. If no symbols are specified, returns orders for all
available markets. Unknown symbols are silently skipped. Optionally
filter by order status. The response includes a `nextCursor` token
when more pages are available — pass it back as `cursor` to continue.

Returns the authenticated wallet's spot portfolio metrics over the
selected timeframe: the spot-equity value series, per-bucket and total
PnL, money-weighted rate of return (MWRR), trading volume, and fees
saved versus a centralized exchange.

The wallet is taken from the bearer token; this endpoint always reports
the caller's own portfolio and requires no `wallet:read_any` scope.

Spot value is the USD value of the wallet's token balances (priced in
USDso, treated as 1 USD); the native token is excluded. PnL is
mark-to-market.

The series ends slightly behind real time to allow for trade-ingestion
latency, and is then snapped down to a fixed bucket-aligned grid: the
end and every bucket boundary fall on whole multiples of the timeframe's
step (1h for `24h`, 6h for `7d`, 1d for `30d` and `all`), aligned to the
UTC epoch. This keeps the grid stable between calls so repeated requests
for the same timeframe return identical bucket timestamps (and are served
from cache) until the newest bucket rolls over. The snapped series end is
reported in `asOf` and equals the timestamp of the last `equity` point.

`asOf` bounds only the equity and PnL series. The `volume` and
`feesSaved` totals are reported as of ingestion latency (real time, not
the grid), so they stay current and timeframe-independent and may include
trades up to one step after `asOf`.
get.summary: Get portfolio metrics for the authenticated wallet

get.description:
Returns the caller's referral status: their own code (if minted), their
aggregate activity as a referrer (referee count, qualified count, and
reward totals by status), and their binding as a referee.

The wallet is taken from the bearer token; this endpoint always reports
the caller's own status. Aggregates only - a referrer never learns which
wallets their referees are; no addresses are returned.
get.summary: Get the authenticated wallet's referral summary

post.description:
Binds the caller (the referee) to the referrer that owns the submitted
code. A referee can be bound at most once, ever. The referrer is resolved
server-side and pinned; the referrer address is never returned.

Responds `201` on a new binding, `200` if the caller was already bound to
the same code (idempotent), `400` for a self-referral, `404` for an
unknown or inactive code, and `409` if the caller is already bound to a
different code.
post.summary: Bind the authenticated wallet to a referral code

get.description:
Returns the caller's referral code. Responds `404` if the caller has not
yet minted one (see the POST on this path).
get.summary: Get the authenticated wallet's referral code

post.description:
Mints an opaque referral code for the caller. Idempotent: a wallet has at
most one code, so if the caller already has one it is returned with `200`
rather than an error. The code is server-generated and opaque; the owner
address is never derivable from it.
post.summary: Mint the authenticated wallet's referral code

get.description:
Returns the authenticated user's pending stop orders across one or
more markets, newest-first. If no symbols are specified, returns
stop orders for all available markets. Unknown symbols are silently
skipped. Optionally filter by status. The response includes a
`nextCursor` token when more pages are available — pass it back as
`cursor` to continue.

Returns 24-hour OHLCV market statistics for one or more markets.
If no symbols are specified, returns tickers for all available markets.

When symbols are supplied and any of them is not a known market, the
whole request is rejected with `400 invalid_param` and the offending
symbols are listed in the error's `context.invalid_symbols` array.
Fail-fast — clients see typos immediately rather than getting a
shorter list back with no way to tell why. The all-markets path (no
symbols filter) has no input to validate and never returns 400.

Returns the authenticated account's executed trades across one or more
markets, where the account was either the taker or the maker. If no
symbols are specified, returns trades for all available markets. Unknown
symbols are silently skipped. Each trade carries its market symbol so
results from different markets can be told apart. Trades are returned
newest-first (reverse chronological order). The `limit` bounds the total
number of trades returned across all markets.

Returns recent executed trades across one or more markets, aggregated
over all traders. If no symbols are specified, returns trades for all
available markets. Unknown symbols are silently skipped. Each trade
carries its market symbol so results from different markets can be told
apart. Trades are returned newest-first (reverse chronological order).
The `limit` bounds the total number of trades returned across all
markets.

The endpoint is public, but callers presenting a bearer token with the
`trades:read_any` scope additionally receive the `maker` and `taker`
wallet addresses on each trade.

Returns the on-chain wallet balances and vault balances for the
given wallet address across all markets. For each market, the
response includes the base and quote token balances in both the
wallet (ERC-20 or native balance) and the vault (withdrawable
balance).

All balances are read at the same block to ensure a consistent
snapshot. When `blockNumber` is omitted, the server fetches the
current block and pins all reads to it. The response includes the
block number used.

Any authenticated caller may read their own wallet. Reading a
different wallet requires the `wallet:read_any` scope; without it,
requesting another wallet returns 403 and an unauthenticated
request returns 401.

Returns whether a wallet address is on the compliance
deny-list. Requires the `screening:read_any` scope.

Resolves a signer / login externally-owned account (EOA) to the smart
wallet(s) provisioned for the owning user. dreamDEX keys on-chain
activity (orders, balances, volume) by the smart wallet address, while
users authenticate with their EOA; this endpoint bridges the two.

The mapping is looked up against the authoritative wallet provider, so
it resolves even for counterfactual (not-yet-deployed) smart wallets.

Returns `200` with a `smartWallets` array that is empty when the EOA is
unknown or has no smart wallet provisioned yet; both cases mean "no
smart wallet right now". Access is restricted to bearer tokens carrying
the `wallet:read_any` scope; tokens without it receive `403`.
get.summary: Resolve smart wallets for an EOA

get.description:
Returns the total trading volume for the given wallet address,
broken down by market. Volume includes trades where the wallet
was either the taker or the maker. Each market entry includes
base volume (sum of trade quantities) and quote volume (sum of
trade costs).

Any authenticated caller may read their own wallet. Reading a
different wallet requires the `wallet:read_any` scope; without it,
requesting another wallet returns 403 and an unauthenticated
request returns 401.

`until` defaults to the current time if omitted; `since` defaults
to `until - 7 days`. The range must not exceed 40 days.
